58.2 First Capital Holdings- Group
a. The Company has provided corporate guarantees for banking facilities obtained by its subsidiaries, First Capital
Limited and First Capital Treasuries PLC, and its parent company, Janashakthi PLC, amounting to LKR 800 Mn,
LKR 1 Bn, and LKR 2 Bn, respectively.
b. The company’s appeal against the assessment on VAT on financial services amounting to LKR 21M (2016/17) is heard
at the Tax Appeals Commission. The appeal against the assessment on VAT on financial services of LKR 233Mn related
to 2017/18 is contested at the Court of Appeal. Further, the Department of Inland Revenue (IRD) raised assessments

Committee.
The review identified follwing matters relating to prior periods, which have been corrected retrospectively in accordance
with LKAS 8 Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors (IAS 8) refer note (65.2-65.5)
1. Consolidation adjustments relating to non-controlling interests (NCI) and indirect holdings – the reversal of a
consolidation entry recorded twice in the year ended 31 March 2018, which had overstated NCI, and the elimination
of fair value gains on shares of Group companies held by First Capital Holdings PLC (Note 65.2).
2. Corrections made by Janashakthi Finance PLC (“JF”) – a subsidiary that reviewed and corrected certain balances in its
own financial statements (Note 65.3).

65.2 Consolidation adjustments: non-controlling interests and indirect holdings
The consolidation correction comprises of two broad categories comprising the following errors, set out in (a) and (b) below
and presented together in the “Consolidation” column of the tables in Note 65.4.1. Together they increase equity attributable
to equity holders of the Company by LKR 949 million at 1 April 2024 (31 March 2025: LKR 599 million) and reduce NCI by LKR
1,541 million (31 March 2025: LKR 1,605 million). Neither element has any effect on the Group’s cash flows.

Janashakthi PLC | Finan cial Statem ents 2025/26   129
(b) Elimination of fair value gains on indirect holdings
First Capital Holdings PLC (“FCH”), a subsidiary of the Company, holds equity interests of 5.78% in Janashakthi Insurance
PLC, with an investment cost of LKR 324 million, and 1.01% in Janashakthi Finance PLC, with an investment cost of LKR
32 million, representing a combined investment cost of approximately LKR 357 million. In FCH’s standalone financial
statements, both investments are measured at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL).

The elimination has now been recorded for all affected periods. It reduces Group retained earnings by LKR 453 million as
of 1 April 2024 which comprise LKR 179 mn due to reversal of fair value gains and LKR 273 mn from removal of indirect
holdings in FCH., and by LKR 349 million for the year ended 31 March 2025. Cumulatively, the elimination reduces Group
investment in financial assets by 1,005 million and both group and company retained earnings by LKR 599 million.
